title: Duleep returns to Sikhi, 1886
hookLine: stopped at Aden on his way to India, he takes amrit again

cards: Officials climb aboard a steamer that has just tied up at a hot, rocky port where ships bound for India stop to take on coal. They have orders for one of the passengers: he may go no further. The port is Aden.
The passenger, traveling east with his family, is Duleep Singh. He has left England and set out for India, and he has told the Sikhs he is coming. He will never reach them.
But in this port, something happens anyway.

teach.b: After his mother's stories, Duleep Singh began to read about the Sikh faith and about the annexation. He came to believe the terms that took his kingdom were unjust, and that the British owed him more than his allowance.
He grew bitter, and he decided to go back to India and to the faith of his father. He set out by sea, writing openly to the Sikhs that he was returning to them.
The British government did not want him in India, where he might become a rallying point, so he was stopped at Aden.

There, in a foreign port, he took amrit, the Khalsa initiation, from Sikhs who had come for it. The man who had been baptized a Christian as a boy was initiated as a Sikh as a grown man. He never reached the Punjab.
In the Anand Sahib, Guru Amar Das opens with a cry of joy addressed to his mother: joy has come, mother, for I have found the true Guru.
A mother who told her son who he was, and a son who came back to it, in the place where he was told he could go no further.
Look back at the week: bandhan, moh, the boy at Fatehgarh, the house in Suffolk, a mother found again and then lost. All week the story has moved away from the Punjab.
Today, in the port where he was stopped, it turns toward it.

how: Sikhs take amrit, the Khalsa initiation, in a ceremony led by initiated Sikhs, and Duleep Singh's initiation at Aden is remembered as his return to the faith of his parents.

games.q: you're Duleep Singh. officials at Aden tell you you may go no further toward India. what do you do there, as the histories tell it?
o: give up and sail back to England quietly.

games.why: he took amrit at Aden; he never reached the Punjab, but he had come back to Sikhi.

practice: Bring to mind one thing you once loved and let go of, a practice, a language, a friend, a place, a habit of kindness, and without judging yourself for leaving it, picture what coming back would look like in the smallest way: one page, one phone call, one quiet minute.
Breathe with that picture, and if you pray, let Waheguru come with each breath.

wordCard.voice: Amrit, the nectar of the Khalsa initiation: stopped at Aden on his way to India, Duleep Singh took it and came back to the faith of his father and mother. Today's word.

orig.note: amrit, the nectar of the Khalsa initiation; taking amrit is how a Sikh joins the Khalsa.

carryVoice: Your line: he came back. Not all the way home, but back all the same. Day nine hundred forty-five.
